ftm.office_address: 4110 Chain Bridge Road, Suite 401, Fairfax, VA 22030
ftm.notes: Probate records are public. Appointments are recommended for in-person research. Notice to Creditors opens the claim window and names the decedent + personal representative; probate rarely carries the property address (a separate assessor lookup fills it). Contact the personal representative / executor, never the deceased.

ftm.data_type: Foreclosure (first public signal for this state's process)
ftm.office_official: Fairfax Circuit Court Land Records Division
ftm.notes: Virginia is a nonjudicial foreclosure state. The first signal is a recorder-filed notice of default or a published trustee-sale notice, which hits the recorder index BEFORE the newspaper ad. Pull the recorder's trustee-sale filings. Online access to scanned indexes and images is available.

ftm.data_type: Recorder / Register of Deeds - Lien & Deed Index
ftm.office_official: Fairfax Circuit Court Land Records Division
ftm.notes: Records documents for property transactions including mechanic's, IRS & state tax, HOA, child-support liens, and lis pendens. Online access to scanned indexes and images is available. Tax and child-support liens are indexed against the PERSON, not the parcel - name-match to the assessor roll. Research Room is open to the public from 8:00 a.m. until 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.

ftm.office_address: 12000 Government Center Parkway, Suite 223, Fairfax, VA 22035
ftm.notes: Virginia is a tax deed state. Auctions of real estate properties are initiated when all other collection attempts have failed. Sales only occur at public auction, typically online. The list publishes as a legal notice weeks before the sale; market the owner before the auction. Any tax sale would be handled by the county's contracted legal firm.

ftm.office_address: 12000 Government Center Parkway, Suite 223, Fairfax, VA 22035
ftm.notes: The county publishes information regarding properties subject to tax sale, which serves as a delinquent roll. Owners owe but no auction date yet. Contact the Department of Tax Administration for current delinquent lists.

ftm.office_official: City of Fairfax Commissioner of the Revenue
ftm.notes: The City of Fairfax provides quarterly updates on delinquent taxes, including real estate. This is a separate list from the county's.

ftm.office_official: Fairfax County Department of Code Compliance
ftm.office_address: 12055 Government Center Parkway, Suite 1016, Fairfax, VA 22035
ftm.notes: Investigates neighborhood quality of life complaints, involving most zoning, noise, property maintenance, building, and fire code violations in unincorporated areas. Records can be requested via email or phone. Online portal for notices of violation (NOVs) exists.

ftm.office_official: Fairfax County Department of Code Compliance
ftm.office_address: 12055 Government Center Parkway, Suite 1016, Fairfax, VA 22035
ftm.notes: The Department of Code Compliance has a Spot Blight Abatement Program to compel demolition or repair if the property owner doesn't address violations voluntarily. Residential demolition permits are also handled by Land Development Services (703-222-0801).
The City of Fairfax handles code administration for properties within its jurisdiction. Contact them directly for records. Office hours: Monday-Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Eviction (Unlawful Detainer) cases are filed in the General District Court. The Virginia Courts Online Case Information System allows searching by plaintiff or defendant name. Hunt the PLAINTIFF (landlord), not the tenant; 2+ filings in 12 months = a tired landlord. The first court action is when a landlord files an unlawful detainer (UD).

ftm_narrative: Data gaps to know about: SiftMap data (provider data) is low or zero in Fairfax County, VA for: Foreclosure notices, Tax sale list, Tax delinquent roll, Probate filings. These are proven deal-makers nationally, and nobody can buy them here, so the county pulls below are not a backup, they are the only way in: treat them as priority pulls. Also not in SiftMap here: Eviction filings, Code violations, Divorce filings.
Sources pulled straight from the county the day records publish, 30 to 90 days before paid data. 'Verify locally' means confirm the link before you work it.

read_me.Doors/deal: Live list size divided by the deals that list produced in the window. Lower is better: fewer doors to work per closed deal.
read_me.Lift: County baseline doors/deal divided by the signal's doors/deal. 3.0 means three times sharper than pulling the whole county.
read_me.Baseline: The whole county unfiltered, counted the same way; the denominator every signal is judged against.
read_me.Stack: Records sitting on two distress lists at once. Stacks are distress plus distress; AI is never AND-stacked on distress.
read_me.AI score: DataSift Investor AI likelihood-to-sell score, 0-100, a PARALLEL pull alongside the distress lists.
read_me.score-gated: Live AI-scored supply counts are provisioned per account, so a local doors/deal cannot be computed in this view. The deals and coverage are this county's own data.
read_me.Verify supply: The row tripped the verify rule (v2.1 coverage-aware: verify reasons annotate (churn: doors/deal < 5; small: list < 250) without demoting; only judicial notice lists and churn artifacts (doors/deal < 1) force P3. Volume floors: P1 needs >=2% of county deal flow or >=25 deals, P2 >=1% or >=12 deals): demand is real, treat the efficiency as directional until you price the live list.
read_me.Evidence A / B / C: from this county's own sold deals / cross-market benchmark / single-market anchor (Knox + Blount TN AI measurement)
read_me.Typical gross: Median of AVM value minus purchase price on clean deals: acquisition spread, not net profit.
read_me.Non-disclosure states: Sale prices are not public there, so deal-dollar columns are omitted; doors/deal and lift never use dollars.
